ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.5 meters. It is brown with dark, speckled markings and a highly elongated, pointed snout. It features a horizontal pupil and a distinctively thin, vine-like body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ahaetulla pulverulenta* is uniquely identified by its extremely elongated, pointed snout that is significantly longer than the diameter of its eye, distinguishing it from other Indian vine snakes.
ai.habitat: The Brown Vine Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found in dense canopy vegetation at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Brown Vine Snake is primarily diurnal, using its slender, cryptic body and binocular vision to actively hunt lizards and frogs among forest foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ahaetulla pulverulenta* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–9 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ahaetulla pulverulenta* occurs in the Western Ghats of India and Sri Lanka, typically inhabiting moist forests from sea level up to approximately 1,500 meters.
